title: Kingdom Hearts III Took 13 Years and Two Game Engines
hook:
Kingdom Hearts II shipped a million copies in three days back in 2005, and then fans waited 13 years for the next numbered game, with a director swap and a whole engine change in the middle. Was Kingdom Hearts III worth the wait?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.

script: Did you know fans waited thirteen years between Kingdom Hearts Two and Kingdom Hearts Three? Kingdom Hearts Two came out in Japan on December twenty second, two thousand five, and shipped a million copies in three days. It reached North America in March of two thousand six and sold another million there in four weeks. Then the numbered series went quiet. Kingdom Hearts Three was finally announced at Sony's E3 press conference in June of two thousand thirteen. The trouble was that director Tetsuya Nomura was also directing Final Fantasy Fifteen, a project he had led for eight years. In September of two thousand fourteen, Square Enix handed Final Fantasy Fifteen to Hajime Tabata so Nomura could focus on Kingdom Hearts. A few weeks later Nomura revealed the team had dropped Square Enix's own Luminous engine and moved the game to Unreal Engine Four. That switch caused rendering problems the team had to work through. After all of that, the finished game finally arrived on PlayStation Four and Xbox One in January of two thousand nineteen. It shipped more than five million copies in its first week, the fastest start in the history of the series. The whole series has now passed thirty seven million copies sold. So, was Kingdom Hearts Three worth the wait? Follow for more gaming history.
